editorial:
Robert Miller has it all on paper: a billion-dollar hedge fund, a loving family, and a deal that will make him even richer. But behind the polished surface, he's hiding cooked books, a secret affair, and a ticking clock. When a late-night drive with his mistress ends in a deadly crash, he panics and calls on Jimmy, a young man from Harlem he barely knows, to help him cover it up. From there, the movie pulls you into a tense game of lies, police pressure, and family fallout.

Richard Gere is fantastic as Miller, playing a man who is charming, ruthless, and quietly falling apart. The pacing stays tight, and the supporting cast, including Susan Sarandon and Tim Roth, keeps every scene sharp. The story can feel a bit familiar if you've seen other Wall Street thrillers, and some side plots get rushed. Still, it's a smart, grown-up thriller that rewards patient viewers. If you enjoy tense dramas about powerful people making bad choices, stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Miller closes the sale of his company and walks away rich, even though his daughter Brooke has figured out he faked the books. Detective Bryer can't prove Miller caused the crash, so the case stalls. Miller's wife Ellen confronts him, knowing about the affair and the cover-up, and demands a divorce plus a huge settlement. Jimmy refuses to flip on Miller, protecting him. Miller gives a speech about moving forward, but his family is shattered. He escapes legal trouble yet loses everything that actually mattered.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves tense financial thrillers and character-driven dramas.
